The linear models of Study 2 (`3_linearmodels.qmd`) give every participant
their own effects of task difficulty and of illusion strength, and of the two
together, on each parameter of the DDM. This script asks how reliable these
participant-level effects are: how well they tell the participants apart,
given how uncertain each participant's estimate is. Those that do are the
candidates for measuring individual differences in sensitivity to illusions.

Like the other scripts, it never loads a fit. The participants' effects are
summarised on the cluster, from the draws of the best linear model of each
illusion (`compute_grouplevel()` in `server/predictions.R`, run by
`./hpc predict`), and stored in the model's prediction file, which is pulled
with `./hpc pull predictions`. The full fits hold some 70,000 participant-level
parameters each, and were made with brms 2.21.0 (`server/AGENT.md` §3.9).

::: {.callout-warning}
**For now this runs on the 50-participant tests of the Müller-Lyer and
Vertical-Horizontal models** (untransformed, `server/AGENT.md` §6.15): the
pipeline, not the results. Fifty participants estimate neither the variability
between participants nor the reliability well, and the Ebbinghaus test is not
predicted yet.
:::

## Loading

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| error: false

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

# igc_grouplevel_effects: the definitions of the participants' effects
source(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/predictions.R" else "analysis/server/predictions.R")
# igc_linear_ranges: the linear subrange, which the empirical indices are
# computed over, as the models are fitted over it
source(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/models.R" else "analysis/server/models.R")

path <- if (dir.exists("models")) "models/" else "analysis/models/"
data_path <- if (dir.exists("../data")) "../data/" else "data/"

# The prediction file of the best linear model of each illusion: the variant
# (untransformed or transformed, 3_linearmodels.qmd) that the comparison of
# the fits retains. Until the full fits exist, the Müller-Lyer one is the
# 50-participant test of 2026-11-25 (job 11841190, server/AGENT.md 6.15), in a
# directory of its own (pulled with IGC_LOCAL_MODELS, server/hpc), untransformed
# (the user's choice over the √|strength| test, 2026-11-25), and the
# Vertical-Horizontal and Ebbinghaus ones the same test of those illusions. An
# illusion with no file yet is left out.
best_files <- c(
  MullerLyer = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/lin_ddm5_mullerlyer_MullerLyer.rds"),
  VerticalHorizontal = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/",
                              "lin_ddm5_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal.rds"),
  Ebbinghaus = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/lin_ddm5_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus.rds")
)

illusions <- c(MullerLyer = "Müller-Lyer", VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal",
               Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus")
# The model's parameters, as estimate_grouplevel() names them ("conditional"
# is the drift)
parameter_labels <- c(conditional = "Drift", sigmadrift = "Drift Variability", boundary = "Boundary",
                      bias = "Starting Point", ndt = "Non-Decision Time", poutlier = "Outlier Proportion")

best_files <- best_files[file.exists(best_files)]
if (length(best_files) < length(illusions)) {
  message("No linear model yet for: ", paste(setdiff(names(illusions), names(best_files)), collapse = ", "))
}
grouplevel <- imap(best_files, \(file, ill) {
  p <- readRDS(file)
  if (is.null(p$grouplevel)) {
    message(file, " has no participants' effects: re-run `./hpc predict` (predictions.R since 2026-11-25).")
  }
  p$grouplevel
})
grouplevel <- grouplevel[!vapply(grouplevel, is.null, logical(1))]

# The tables, in one style, with the numbers centred in their cells
gt_style <- function(tab) {
  tab |>
    cols_align("center", columns = where(is.numeric)) |>
    tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), heading.title.font.size = px(16),
                heading.subtitle.font.size = px(13), data_row.padding = px(3),
                row_group.font.weight = "bold", row_group.background.color = "#F5F5F5")
}
```

## The Participants' Effects

Each parameter of the linear models has, per participant, a deviation from the
population for each of its terms (the random effects): an intercept, the
difference, the absolute strength, the absolute strength by its direction
(Effect, +0.5 when the illusion is incongruent, −0.5 when it is congruent),
and the interactions of the difference with the last two. The raw terms are
not the most interpretable, since the effect of the strength is split between
`Strength` and `Strength:Effect`. The effects studied here are the baseline of
each parameter (its intercept) and combinations of the other terms, made draw
by draw on the cluster:

```{r}
effect_meanings <- c(
  "Baseline" = "The parameter with no illusion, at the middle difficulty and the centre of the ISI window",
  "Difficulty" = "The effect of the difference between the targets, with no illusion",
  "Strength (incongruent)" = "The slope of the illusion's strength when it is incongruent",
  "Strength (congruent)" = "The slope of the illusion's strength when it is congruent",
  "Difficulty x Strength (incongruent)" = "How the difference changes the slope of an incongruent illusion",
  "Difficulty x Strength (congruent)" = "How the difference changes the slope of a congruent illusion",
  "PSE" = paste0("The difference between the targets at which the drift is zero under an incongruent illusion ",
                 "of medium strength: the difference the illusion cancels (drift only, raw units)")
)
tibble(Effect = names(igc_grouplevel_effects),
       Terms = map_chr(igc_grouplevel_effects, \(w) {
         paste(sprintf("%s%s%s", ifelse(seq_along(w) == 1, "", ifelse(w < 0, " − ", " + ")),
                       ifelse(abs(w) == 1, "", paste0(abs(w), " × ")), names(w)), collapse = "")
       })) |>
  add_row(Effect = "PSE",
          Terms = "−a / g in raw units: a, g the total drift at D = 0 and its slope of D, at half the strongest strength") |>
  mutate(Meaning = effect_meanings[Effect]) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The participants' effects", subtitle = "Per parameter of the model") |>
  gt_style() |>
  cols_align("left")
```

The predictors are coded as in the fits: the difference from −1 to 1 and the
absolute strength from 0 to 1 over the range fitted, so the slope of the
strength is the change from no illusion to the strongest illusion of the range.
Each effect is a deviation of the participant from the population, on the
link scale of its parameter, and the baseline a deviation from the
participant's study, which has an intercept of its own. The outlier proportion
has a baseline only. Baselines can be expected to be the most reliable: every
trial informs them, where a slope rests on the contrast between trials.

The model-based PSE is the one effect that is not a deviation. It is computed
draw by draw from the participant's total coefficients on the drift
(population + study + participant), in the raw units of the difference, at
the same strength as the empirical PSE below (`igc_pse_strength`, half the
strongest of the range). It is the illusion's strength expressed as the
physical difference it cancels. A precision common to all of a participant's
drift coefficients cancels out of it. The raw strength slope keeps that
precision: participants who see differences more sharply have steeper slopes
for real and illusory differences alike. The PSE thus measures susceptibility
relative to the participant's own discrimination.

```{r}
imap_dfr(grouplevel, \(g, ill) {
  g$effects |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(Participants = n_distinct(Level), .by = Component) |>
    mutate(Illusion = illusions[ill])
}) |>
  summarise(Participants = first(Participants), .by = Illusion) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Participants per model") |>
  gt_style()
```

## Reliability: D-vour

D-vour, the variability-over-uncertainty ratio (`performance::performance_dvour()`),
compares how much the participants' estimates differ from one another with
how uncertain each of them is:

$$
\text{D-vour} = \frac{\sigma_B^2}{\sigma_B^2 + \mu_{\text{SE}}^2}
$$

where $\sigma_B$ is the standard deviation, across participants, of their
point estimates (posterior medians), and $\mu_{\text{SE}}$ the mean of their
posterior dispersions (MADs). It is 0 when the differences between
participants are no larger than the uncertainty of each, and tends to 1 when
the uncertainty is negligible next to them. Above 0.75 the differences
between participants are at least three times the uncertainty; around 0.5
the two are similar, and the estimates should be used with caution; below
0.5 the uncertainty dominates (the `performance` documentation). It rests on
the estimates alone, so it is itself more reliable with more participants.

```{r}
# D-vour of every effect of every parameter
dvour_of <- function(tables) {
  imap_dfr(tables, \(g, ill) mutate(performance::performance_dvour(g), Illusion_Type = ill)) |>
    mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
           Model_Parameter = factor(parameter_labels[Component], levels = parameter_labels),
           Effect = Parameter)
}
dvour <- dvour_of(map(grouplevel, "effects")) |>
  mutate(Effect = factor(Effect, levels = igc_grouplevel_effect_names))

# The illusions that have a model, in order
present <- intersect(names(illusions), names(grouplevel))

# An effect is reliable when its D-vour is above the threshold on every
# illusion that has a model. The structure analysis takes these effects, the
# same ones on every illusion.
reliable_threshold <- 0.5
reliable_effects <- dvour |>
  summarise(Lowest = min(D_vour), .by = c(Component, Parameter)) |>
  filter(Lowest > reliable_threshold)
```

### Across Illusions

One row per effect, with its D-vour on each illusion side by side, so that
it shows whether the same effects are reliable on every illusion. The rows
are sorted by the lowest D-vour of the illusions, and those above
`reliable_threshold` on every illusion (bold) are the ones the structure
analysis takes, on every illusion.

```{r}
dvour_colour <- \(x) scales::col_numeric(c("#FFEBEE", "#FFF8E1", "#C8E6C9", "#2E7D32"),
                                        domain = c(0, 1))(pmin(pmax(x, 0), 1))

# One row per effect, a column of D-vour per illusion and the lowest of them,
# from the most to the least reliable on every illusion
dvour_wide <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(Lowest = min(D_vour), .by = c(Component, Parameter)) |>
    select(Illusion_Type, Component, Model_Parameter, Effect, Lowest, D_vour) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Illusion_Type, values_from = D_vour) |>
    arrange(desc(Lowest)) |>
    mutate(Rank = row_number(), Reliable = Lowest > reliable_threshold) |>
    select(Rank, Model_Parameter, Effect, all_of(present), Lowest, Reliable)
}
dvour_gt <- function(w, title, subtitle, effect_label = "Effect", bold = FALSE) {
  tab <- gt(w) |>
    tab_header(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) |>
    tab_spanner("D-vour", columns = c(all_of(present), Lowest)) |>
    cols_label(.list = c(list(Model_Parameter = "Parameter", Effect = effect_label, Lowest = "Lowest"),
                         as.list(illusions[present]))) |>
    fmt_number(c(all_of(present), Lowest), decimals = 2) |>
    data_color(c(all_of(present), Lowest), fn = dvour_colour)
  if (bold) tab <- tab_style(tab, cell_text(weight = "bold"), cells_body(rows = Reliable))
  tab |>
    cols_hide(Reliable) |>
    gt_style()
}

dvour |>
  dvour_wide() |>
  dvour_gt("Reliability of the participants' effects",
           "D-vour per illusion, from the most to the least reliable on every illusion", bold = TRUE) |>
  tab_source_note(paste0("Lowest: the lowest D-vour of the illusions. Bold: above ", reliable_threshold,
                         " on every illusion, the effects of the structure analysis."))
```

```{r}
dvour |>

  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#FFEBEE") +
```

For reference, the D-vour of the raw random effects, every term of every
parameter, the intercepts (and the outlier proportion's) included.

```{r}
dvour_of(map(grouplevel, "terms")) |>
  dvour_wide() |>
  dvour_gt("Reliability of the random effects as fitted",
```

## Empirical Indices

The usual way to measure individual differences in this task is from the
behaviour directly: how often and how fast a participant responds, overall and
when the illusion works against them, and where their psychometric function
lies. These indices are computed here for every participant, on each illusion,
from the trials the linear models are fitted on (the linear subrange,
`igc_linear_ranges`), so that the next section can relate them to the
participants' model parameters, with the same trials behind both.

```{r}
# The indices, in the order of the tables and plots, with what they are
index_definitions <- tribble(
  ~Index, ~Label, ~Definition,
  "Error_Rate", "Error rate", "Proportion of errors, all trials",
  "RT_Median", "Median RT (s)", "Median RT of the correct responses, all trials",
  "IES", "IES (s)", "Inverse efficiency score: mean RT of the correct responses / proportion correct, all trials",
  "Error_Rate_Incongruent", "Error rate, incongruent", "Proportion of errors when the illusion is incongruent",
  "RT_Median_Incongruent", "Median RT, incongruent (s)", "Median RT of the correct responses when the illusion is incongruent",
  "IES_Incongruent", "IES, incongruent (s)", "Inverse efficiency score when the illusion is incongruent",
  "Illusion_Effect_Errors", "Illusion effect on errors", "Error rate, incongruent − congruent",
  "Illusion_Effect_RT", "Illusion effect on RT (s)", "Median correct RT, incongruent − congruent",
  "PSE", "PSE (difference)", "Point of subjective equality of an incongruent illusion of medium strength (half the strongest of the range): the difference between the targets it cancels (50% errors), from the psychometric function",
  "JND", "JND (difference)", "Just-noticeable difference with no illusion: the difference from 50% to 75% correct, from the psychometric function"
)

index_definitions |>
  select(Index = Label, Definition) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Empirical indices", subtitle = "Per participant and illusion, on the trials of the linear subrange") |>
  gt_style() |>
  cols_align("left")
```

The psychometric function is a logistic regression of each participant's
errors on the difference between the targets and the signed strength of the
illusion (positive when incongruent), on one illusion. Where the error rate is
50%, the participant cannot tell the targets apart. With no illusion, the
slope of the difference gives the JND. Under an incongruent illusion, the
difference at which the errors reach 50% is the point of subjective equality:
the physical difference the illusion cancels, in the units of the difference.
It is taken at half the strongest incongruent strength of the range: at the
strongest, it lies beyond the largest difference shown for about one
participant in six on the Müller-Lyer and Vertical-Horizontal illusions, where
it is extrapolated. The function is linear in both predictors, as a first
approximation. It is left missing when the participant made fewer than five
errors or the fit fails, and when it is degenerate. That covers errors that
do not decrease as the difference grows, and a JND beyond the largest
difference shown (the errors barely depend on the difference). It also covers
a JND below a tenth of the smallest (the errors switch from all to none
between two levels, so the slope is not estimable).

```{r}
# Every participant's trials on each illusion, within its linear subrange
# (the rule of igc_linear_data(), which fit_model.R applies)
ranges <- imap_dfr(igc_linear_ranges, \(r, ill) {
  tibble(Illusion_Type = ill, D_lo = r$difference[1], D_hi = r$difference[2], S_max = r$strength)
})
trials <- map_dfr(1:3, \(i) read.csv(paste0(data_path, "illusion_part", i, ".csv"))) |>
  mutate(Illusion_Difference = abs(Illusion_Difference)) |>
  inner_join(ranges, by = "Illusion_Type") |>
  filter(Illusion_Difference >= D_lo - 1e-9, Illusion_Difference <= D_hi + 1e-9,
         abs(Illusion_Strength) <= S_max + 1e-9)

# A participant's psychometric function on one illusion (see above): the PSE
# of an incongruent illusion of half the strongest strength of the range, and
# the JND, or NA when the function is degenerate
psychometric <- function(d, s_max, d_lo, d_hi) {
  na <- c(PSE = NA_real_, JND = NA_real_)
  if (sum(d$Error) < 5) return(na)
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(glm(Error ~ Illusion_Difference + Illusion_Strength,
                                       family = binomial, data = d)),
                  error = \(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit) || !fit$converged) return(na)
  b <- coef(fit)
  if (anyNA(b) || b[["Illusion_Difference"]] >= 0) return(na)
  jnd <- log(3) / -b[["Illusion_Difference"]]
  if (jnd > d_hi || jnd < d_lo / 10) return(na)
  # At the strength of the model-based PSE (igc_pse_strength, server/predictions.R)
  c(PSE = -(b[["(Intercept)"]] + b[["Illusion_Strength"]] * s_max * igc_pse_strength) /
      b[["Illusion_Difference"]],
    JND = jnd)
}

# The inverse efficiency score of some trials (missing if all are errors)
ies <- \(rt, error) if (mean(error) >= 1) NA_real_ else mean(rt[error == 0]) / (1 - mean(error))

empirical <- trials |>
  group_by(Illusion_Type, Participant) |>
  group_modify(\(d, key) {
    inc <- d$Illusion_Strength > 0
    con <- d$Illusion_Strength < 0
    correct <- d$Error == 0
    pf <- psychometric(d, d$S_max[1], d$D_lo[1], d$D_hi[1])
    tibble(Study = sub("^IllusionGame", "", d$Dataset[1]),
           Trials = nrow(d),
           Error_Rate = mean(d$Error),
           RT_Median = median(d$RT[correct]),
           IES = ies(d$RT, d$Error),
           Error_Rate_Incongruent = mean(d$Error[inc]),
           RT_Median_Incongruent = median(d$RT[inc & correct]),
           IES_Incongruent = ies(d$RT[inc], d$Error[inc]),
           Illusion_Effect_Errors = mean(d$Error[inc]) - mean(d$Error[con]),
           Illusion_Effect_RT = median(d$RT[inc & correct]) - median(d$RT[con & correct]),
           PSE = pf[["PSE"]],
           JND = pf[["JND"]])
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions))
```

```{r}
# Per illusion: each index's median and interquartile range across
# participants, and the number of participants it could be computed for
empirical |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(index_definitions$Index), names_to = "Index", values_to = "Value") |>
  summarise(Median = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q1 = quantile(Value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q3 = quantile(Value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            N = sum(!is.na(Value)),
            .by = c(Illusion, Index)) |>
  mutate(Index = factor(index_definitions$Label[match(Index, index_definitions$Index)],
                        levels = index_definitions$Label),
         Summary = sprintf("%.3g [%.3g, %.3g]", Median, Q1, Q3)) |>
  select(Illusion, Index, Summary, N) |>
  arrange(Illusion, Index) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Illusion, values_from = c(Summary, N), names_glue = "{Illusion}__{.value}",
              names_vary = "slowest") |>
  arrange(Index) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Empirical indices", subtitle = "Median [interquartile range] across participants, and N") |>
  tab_spanner_delim("__") |>
  fmt_integer(ends_with("__N")) |>
  gt_style()
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 10

# Their distributions across participants. The axes stop at the 1st and 99th
# percentiles of each index, which the PSE and the JND can exceed by far when a
# psychometric function is nearly flat.
illusion_colours <- c("Müller-Lyer" = "#E91E63", "Vertical-Horizontal" = "#3F51B5", "Ebbinghaus" = "#009688")
empirical |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(index_definitions$Index), names_to = "Index", values_to = "Value") |>
  filter(!is.na(Value)) |>
  mutate(Index = factor(index_definitions$Label[match(Index, index_definitions$Index)],
                        levels = index_definitions$Label)) |>
  filter(between(Value, quantile(Value, 0.01), quantile(Value, 0.99)), .by = Index) |>
  ggplot(aes(Value, fill = Illusion, colour = Illusion)) +

```

The indices are computed for every participant, but only those in a model
(`grouplevel`, above) have parameters to compare them with: for now, the 50
participants of each illusion's test.

```{r}
imap_dfr(grouplevel, \(g, ill) {
  ids <- unique(as.data.frame(g$effects)$Level)
  tibble(Illusion = illusions[[ill]],
         `In the model` = length(ids),
         `With empirical indices` = sum(ids %in% empirical$Participant[empirical$Illusion_Type == ill]))
}) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Participants in both") |>
  gt_style()
```

## Structure Analysis

How the model's participant-level effects relate to one another and to the
empirical indices, on each illusion: one correlation matrix per illusion, of
the model effects reliable on every illusion (a D-vour above
`reliable_threshold` on each, above) and the empirical indices, over the
participants of that illusion's model. The matrices hold the same variables,
in the same order, so that they can be compared cell by cell. The question is
whether the structure is the same on every illusion. The order is a
hierarchical clustering of the absolute correlations averaged over the
illusions (`correlation::cor_sort()` on 1 − mean |r|), so that variables that
go together sit together, whether they rise or fall together.

Three choices:
- The correlations are Spearman's, since several indices are skewed (RTs,
  IES, the PSE and JND).
- Every variable is centred within the participant's study first, on each
  illusion. The model's baselines are deviations from the study's intercept,
  while the empirical indices also carry the differences between studies.
  Centring both leaves the differences between participants of the same study
  only, on both sides.
- The illusions are not in the same matrix. Correlating them, participant by
  participant, is for the dimension scores, once they are extracted from
  these matrices. It needs the participants of one illusion's model to be in
  the others' too, which the full fits will have (the tests drew their 50
  participants on each illusion independently).

The empirical indices have no reliability of their own here, so a weak
correlation with one of them may only mean that it is noisy.

```{r}
center_within_study <- TRUE

# Each participant's model effects (posterior medians), long, for the effects
# reliable on every illusion
model_scores <- imap_dfr(grouplevel, \(g, ill) mutate(as.data.frame(g$effects), Illusion_Type = ill)) |>
  semi_join(reliable_effects, by = c("Component", "Parameter")) |>
  transmute(Participant = Level, Illusion_Type, Source = "Model",
            Variable = paste0(parameter_labels[Component], ": ", Parameter), Value = Median)

# Their empirical indices, on the illusions that have a model, for the
# participants in it
empirical_scores <- empirical |>
  filter(Illusion_Type %in% names(grouplevel)) |>
  semi_join(distinct(model_scores, Participant, Illusion_Type), by = c("Participant", "Illusion_Type")) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(index_definitions$Index), names_to = "Index", values_to = "Value") |>
  transmute(Participant, Illusion_Type, Source = "Empirical",
            Variable = index_definitions$Label[match(Index, index_definitions$Index)], Value)

# Every participant's study, from the empirical indices (every participant
# has them)
studies_of <- distinct(empirical, Participant, Study)

# Centred within study, on each illusion
structure_long <- bind_rows(model_scores, empirical_scores) |>
  left_join(studies_of, by = "Participant") |>
  mutate(Value = if (center_within_study) Value - mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE) else Value,
         .by = c(Illusion_Type, Variable, Study))

# The variables, the same on every illusion
variables <- unique(structure_long$Variable)
sources <- distinct(structure_long, Variable, Source)

# Per illusion, one row per participant of its model, the variables in the
# order of `variables`
structure_wide <- map(set_names(present), \(ill) {
  structure_long |>
    filter(Illusion_Type == ill) |>
    select(Participant, Variable, Value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Variable, values_from = Value) |>
    select(Participant, all_of(variables))
})

# One matrix per illusion: Spearman correlations, pairwise, over the
# participants of its model
cors <- map(structure_wide, \(w) cor(w[variables], method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
n_participants <- map_int(structure_wide, nrow)

# One order for every illusion: hierarchical clustering of the absolute
# correlations averaged over the illusions. The distance between two variables
# is 1 - mean |r|, so that strongly related ones sit together whatever the
# sign of the relation (cor_sort()'s default, (1 - r) / 2, would put r = -.9
# as far apart as possible). Each signed matrix is then shown in that order.
mean_abs <- apply(simplify2array(map(cors, abs)), c(1, 2), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
order_vars <- rownames(correlation::cor_sort(1 - mean_abs, distance = "raw"))
```

```{r}
dvour |>
  semi_join(reliable_effects, by = c("Component", "Parameter")) |>
  dvour_wide() |>
  dvour_gt("The model effects in the matrices",
           paste0("D-vour above ", reliable_threshold, " on every illusion, with the ",
                  nrow(index_definitions), " empirical indices"))
```

```{r}
# One illusion's matrix, in the common order (order_vars)
plot_structure <- function(ill) {
  r <- cors[[ill]][order_vars, order_vars]
  as.data.frame(r) |>
    rownames_to_column("Variable1") |>
    pivot_longer(-Variable1, names_to = "Variable2", values_to = "r") |>
    mutate(Label = if_else(Variable1 == Variable2, "", sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf("%.2f", r))),
           Variable1 = factor(Variable1, levels = rev(order_vars)),
           Variable2 = factor(Variable2, levels = order_vars)) |>
    ggplot(aes(Variable2, Variable1, fill = r)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Label, colour = abs(r) > 0.6), size = 2.4, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1565C0", mid = "white", high = "#C62828", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "rho") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey20", "TRUE" = "white")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         title = paste0(illusions[[ill]], ": structure of the model effects and the empirical indices"),
         subtitle = paste0("Spearman correlations, ", n_participants[[ill]], " participants",
                           if (center_within_study) ", centred within study" else "",
                           "; ", sum(sources$Source == "Model"), " model effects (D-vour > ",
                           reliable_threshold, " on every illusion) and ", sum(sources$Source == "Empirical"),
                           " empirical indices")) +
    coord_equal() +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

```

One tab per illusion, every matrix in the same order:

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8.5

for (ill in present) {
  cat("\n\n### ", illusions[[ill]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(plot_structure(ill))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

:::

### Is the Structure the Same on Every Illusion?

For each pair of illusions: the correlation, over every pair of variables, of
their correlation on one illusion with their correlation on the other (1 when
the two matrices are the same up to a linear rescaling), and the mean
absolute difference between the two. Also the number of participants the two
models share, over whom dimension scores could be correlated (next section).

```{r}
if (length(present) < 2) {
  message("One illusion only: nothing to compare yet.")
} else {
  low <- lower.tri(cors[[1]])
  ids <- map(grouplevel[present], \(g) unique(as.data.frame(g$effects)$Level))
  combn(present, 2, simplify = FALSE) |>
    map_dfr(\(p) {
      a <- cors[[p[1]]][low]
      b <- cors[[p[2]]][low]
      tibble(Illusions = paste(illusions[p], collapse = " – "),
             Similarity = cor(a, b, use = "complete.obs"),
             Difference = mean(abs(a - b), na.rm = TRUE),
             Shared = length(intersect(ids[[p[1]]], ids[[p[2]]])))
    }) |>
    gt() |>
    tab_header(title = "The structure across illusions",
               subtitle = paste0("Over the ", sum(low), " pairs of variables of the matrices")) |>
    cols_label(Illusions = "", Similarity = "Correlation of the correlations",
               Difference = "Mean absolute difference", Shared = "Participants in both models") |>
    fmt_number(c(Similarity, Difference), decimals = 2) |>
    fmt_integer(Shared) |>
    gt_style()
}
```

## Dimensions

The matrices above show blocks of variables that go together. This section
makes them dimensions and asks whether they are the same on every illusion,
in two steps:
- **Exploratory Graph Analysis** (EGA) finds the dimensions of each illusion,
  and how stable they are.
- **A confirmatory factor analysis** (CFA) of the structure common to the
  illusions tests whether it holds on each illusion and across illusions,
  and gives each participant a score on each dimension, illusion by illusion.

On the 50-participant tests this sets up the pipeline only. EGA and its
bootstraps are unstable at that size, and the cross-illusion analyses need
the same participants in every model, which only the full fits will have.

```{r}
# Unique Variable Analysis: the weighted topological overlap above which two
# variables are redundant (EGAnet's default)
uva_cutoff <- 0.25
# Resamples of the participants for the stability of EGA
boot_iter <- 500
# The cross-illusion analyses need at least this many participants in every
# model
min_shared <- 200
illusion_codes <- c(MullerLyer = "ML", VerticalHorizontal = "VH", Ebbinghaus = "Ebb")
```

### Redundant Variables

Several variables are near-duplicates: the drift's baseline and difficulty,
or the median RT of incongruent trials and the illusion effect on RT, which
is computed from it. A pair that shares most of its connections in the
network forms a dimension of its own, and inflates the one it belongs to.
Unique Variable Analysis (`EGAnet::UVA()`) flags the pairs whose weighted
topological overlap (wTO) exceeds `uva_cutoff`. Of each redundant set, it
keeps the variable least redundant with the rest (the lowest maximum wTO with
the other variables). It is run on each illusion, and a variable it removes
on any illusion is removed on every illusion, so that every illusion keeps
the same variables.

```{r}
uva <- map(structure_wide, \(w) {
  EGAnet::UVA(as.data.frame(w[variables]), corr = "spearman", cut.off = uva_cutoff,
              reduce = TRUE, reduce.method = "remove")
})
uva_removed <- unique(unlist(map(uva, \(u) u$keep_remove$remove)))
conflicts <- intersect(uva_removed, unique(unlist(map(uva, \(u) u$keep_remove$keep))))
if (length(conflicts) > 0) {
  message("Kept on one illusion but removed on another (removed on every illusion): ",
          paste(conflicts, collapse = ", "))
}

# The variables of the dimensions, in the order of the matrices
dim_vars <- setdiff(order_vars, uva_removed)

wto_colour <- \(x) scales::col_numeric(c("white", "#FFE0B2", "#E65100"), domain = c(0, 0.5))(pmin(pmax(x, 0), 0.5))

# Every pair above the threshold on at least one illusion, with its wTO on
# each illusion and the variable removed
imap_dfr(uva, \(u, ill) mutate(u$wto$pairwise, Illusion_Type = ill)) |>
  mutate(A = pmin(node_i, node_j), B = pmax(node_i, node_j)) |>
  select(Illusion_Type, A, B, wto) |>
  filter(any(wto > uva_cutoff), .by = c(A, B)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Illusion_Type, values_from = wto) |>
  mutate(Removed = case_when(A %in% uva_removed & B %in% uva_removed ~ "both",
                             A %in% uva_removed ~ A,
                             B %in% uva_removed ~ B,
                             .default = "neither"),
         Highest = do.call(pmax, c(across(all_of(present)), na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  arrange(desc(Highest)) |>
  select(-Highest) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Redundant variables",
             subtitle = paste0("Pairs with a wTO above ", uva_cutoff, " on at least one illusion")) |>
  tab_spanner("wTO", columns = all_of(present)) |>
  cols_label(.list = c(list(A = "Variable", B = "Redundant with"), as.list(illusions[present]))) |>
  fmt_number(all_of(present), decimals = 2) |>
  data_color(all_of(present), fn = wto_colour) |>
  tab_source_note(paste0("Removed: the variable left out on every illusion. ", length(dim_vars), " of ",
                         length(variables), " variables remain.")) |>
  gt_style()
```

### Exploratory Graph Analysis

EGA (`EGAnet::EGA()`) estimates a network of the variables (a GLASSO
network of their Spearman correlations) and takes its communities (walktrap)
as the dimensions. Their number comes from the data, and every variable
belongs to one.

- **Stability.** `EGAnet::bootEGA()` re-estimates it on `boot_iter`
  resamples of each illusion's participants. It gives how often each number
  of dimensions comes up, and how often each variable falls in its own
  dimension (item stability; above 0.75 is usually taken as stable).
- **The common structure** is the EGA of the illusions pooled, each variable
  standardised within its illusion. Each illusion's dimensions are matched
  to it by their overlap, and each dimension is named after its variable with
  the highest network loading in the pooled analysis.

```{r}
# Each illusion: EGA (a GLASSO network of the Spearman correlations, walktrap
# communities), and its stability over resamples of the participants
reduced <- map(structure_wide, \(w) as.data.frame(w[dim_vars]))
boot <- map(reduced, \(d) {
  EGAnet::bootEGA(d, corr = "spearman", model = "glasso", algorithm = "walktrap", iter = boot_iter,
                  type = "resampling", seed = 2026, plot.itemStability = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
})
ega <- map(boot, "EGA")

# The common structure: EGA of the illusions pooled
ega_all <- EGAnet::EGA(map_dfr(reduced, \(d) as.data.frame(scale(d))), corr = "spearman", model = "glasso",
                       algorithm = "walktrap", plot.EGA = FALSE)
common <- ega_all$wc
# (net.loads() prints a notice of EGAnet's change of default even when
# loading.method is given)
loads_all <- suppressMessages(EGAnet::net.loads(ega_all, loading.method = "revised"))$std
dims <- split(names(common), common)
dim_labels <- imap_chr(dims, \(v, k) paste0("D", k, " (", v[which.max(abs(loads_all[v, k]))], ")"))

# An illusion's communities relabelled with the common ones they overlap most
# (greedily, the largest overlap first); one that matches none is "other"
match_communities <- function(wc, ref) {
  tab <- table(wc, ref[names(wc)])
  lab <- setNames(rep(NA_character_, nrow(tab)), rownames(tab))
  while (length(tab) > 0 && max(tab) > 0) {
    ij <- which(tab == max(tab), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
    lab[rownames(tab)[ij[1]]] <- colnames(tab)[ij[2]]
    tab[ij[1], ] <- 0
    tab[, ij[2]] <- 0
  }
  out <- unname(lab[as.character(wc)])
  out[is.na(out) & !is.na(wc)] <- "other"
  setNames(out, names(wc))
}
matched <- map(ega, \(e) match_communities(e$wc, common))
```

```{r}
# The number of dimensions on each illusion, its stability, and how far the
# illusion's dimensions agree with the common ones
imap_dfr(boot, \(b, ill) {
  f <- b$frequency
  tibble(Illusion = illusions[[ill]],
         Dimensions = b$EGA$n.dim,
         Boot_median = b$summary.table$median.dim,
         Boot_range = paste0(b$summary.table$Lower.Quantile, "–", b$summary.table$Upper.Quantile),
         Boot_same = sum(f$Frequency[f[[1]] == b$EGA$n.dim]),
         Agreement = mean(matched[[ill]] == common[names(matched[[ill]])], na.rm = TRUE))
}) |>
  add_row(Illusion = "All (pooled)", Dimensions = ega_all$n.dim) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The dimensions of each illusion",
             subtitle = paste0("EGA, and over ", boot_iter, " resamples of the participants")) |>
  tab_spanner("Resamples", c(Boot_median, Boot_range, Boot_same)) |>
  cols_label(Boot_median = "Median", Boot_range = "95% range", Boot_same = "Same number",
             Agreement = "Variables in the common dimension") |>
  fmt_percent(c(Boot_same, Agreement), decimals = 0) |>
  sub_missing() |>
  gt_style()

# Each variable: its common dimension, and on each illusion the dimension it
# falls in (matched to the common ones) and its item stability
stability <- map(boot, \(b) EGAnet::itemStability(b, IS.plot = FALSE)$item.stability$empirical.dimensions)
dim_name <- \(k) if_else(k %in% names(dims), paste0("D", k), k)
imap_dfr(matched, \(m, ill) {
  tibble(Variable = names(m), Illusion = illusions[[ill]], Dimension = dim_name(m),
         Stability = unname(stability[[ill]][names(m)]))
}) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Illusion, values_from = c(Dimension, Stability),
              names_glue = "{Illusion}__{.value}", names_vary = "slowest") |>
  mutate(Common = dim_labels[as.character(common[Variable])], .after = Variable) |>
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = dim_vars)) |>
  arrange(Common, Variable) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Common") |>
  tab_header(title = "The variables in the dimensions",
             subtitle = "Grouped by their common dimension; per illusion, their dimension and item stability") |>
  tab_spanner_delim("__") |>
  fmt_number(ends_with("__Stability"), decimals = 2) |>
  data_color(ends_with("__Stability"), fn = dvour_colour) |>
  tab_source_note("Dimension: as matched to the common ones (\"other\": an extra dimension of that illusion).") |>
  gt_style()
```

The networks, with the dimensions coloured as matched to the common ones, so
that the same colour is the same dimension in every tab:

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

# One colour per dimension number. EGAnet colours the communities by rank, so
# each plot gets the colours of the numbers it has.
dim_palette <- c("#F03D2D", "#90DDF0", "#C8D96F", "#9C27B0", "#FF9800", "#795548", "#607D8B", "#E91E63")
networks <- c(list(All = ega_all), ega)
for (n in names(networks)) {
  e <- networks[[n]]
  if (n != "All") {
    m <- matched[[n]][names(e$wc)]
    # The common dimensions keep their number; an extra one takes the next
    e$wc[] <- if_else(m == "other", length(dims) + 1, suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m)))
  }
  cat("\n\n### ", if (n == "All") "All illusions (pooled)" else illusions[[n]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(plot(e, color.palette = dim_palette[sort(unique(na.omit(as.numeric(e$wc))))]))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

:::

### Confirmatory Factor Analysis

The common structure as a CFA (`lavaan::cfa()`): each variable loads on its
dimension only, the dimensions are correlated, and the variables are
standardised within the illusion. It is estimated by robust maximum
likelihood (MLR), with full-information maximum likelihood for the missing
values (a JND that could not be computed).

- **On each illusion**: whether the common structure fits it. CFI and TLI
  above .95, RMSEA below .06 and SRMR below .08 are the usual marks of a good
  fit. "Admissible" is false when an estimate is out of bounds, such as a
  negative residual variance.
- **Across illusions**: one model of every illusion's variables, over the
  participants in every model, with the residuals of each variable
  correlated across illusions (the same participant). The configural model
  (the same structure on every illusion) is compared with the metric model
  (the same loadings too), by the scaled χ² difference and the change in CFI
  (a drop of more than .01 is usually read as non-invariance). Scalar
  invariance is not tested, since every variable is centred within study on
  each illusion and so has a mean of 0 by construction.

```{r}
# lavaan needs syntactic names
codes <- setNames(paste0("x", seq_along(dim_vars)), dim_vars)

# The model of the common structure for the illusions given by their suffixes
# ("" for one illusion alone). `equal`: the loadings equal across illusions
# (each dimension keeps its first variable as the marker). A dimension with one
# variable is that variable.
cfa_syntax <- function(suffixes, equal = FALSE) {
  lines <- c()
  for (s in suffixes) {
    for (k in names(dims)) {
      v <- codes[dims[[k]]]
      lab <- if (equal) paste0("l", k, "_", v, "*") else ""
      lines <- c(lines, paste0("D", k, s, " =~ ", paste0(lab, v, s, collapse = " + ")))
      if (length(v) == 1) lines <- c(lines, paste0(v, s, " ~~ 0*", v, s))
    }
  }
  if (length(suffixes) > 1) {
    v <- codes[unlist(dims)]
    for (p in combn(suffixes, 2, simplify = FALSE)) {
      lines <- c(lines, paste0(v, p[1], " ~~ ", v, p[2]))
    }
  }
  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}
fit_cfa <- function(model, data) {
  suppressWarnings(lavaan::cfa(model, data = data, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml"))
}
fit_indices <- function(f) {
  i <- c("cfi.robust", "tli.robust", "rmsea.robust", "srmr")
  ok <- lavaan::lavInspect(f, "converged")
  x <- if (ok) lavaan::fitMeasures(f, i) else setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(i)), i)
  tibble(Participants = lavaan::lavInspect(f, "nobs"), CFI = x[[1]], TLI = x[[2]], RMSEA = x[[3]],
         SRMR = x[[4]], Converged = ok,
         Admissible = ok && isTRUE(suppressWarnings(lavaan::lavInspect(f, "post.check"))))
}

# Each illusion on its own
cfa_data <- map(reduced, \(d) setNames(as.data.frame(scale(d)), codes[names(d)]))
cfa_fits <- map(cfa_data, \(d) fit_cfa(cfa_syntax(""), d))

imap_dfr(cfa_fits, \(f, ill) mutate(fit_indices(f), Model = illusions[[ill]], .before = 1)) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The common structure on each illusion", subtitle = "CFA, robust fit indices") |>
  cols_label(Model = "") |>
  fmt_number(c(CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR), decimals = 3) |>
  gt_style()
```

```{r}
# Across illusions: the participants in every model
shared <- Reduce(intersect, map(structure_wide, "Participant"))
if (length(present) < 2 || length(shared) < min_shared) {
  message("The invariance across illusions needs at least ", min_shared, " participants in every model (",
          length(shared), " now): the full fits.")
} else {
  suffixes <- setNames(paste0("_", illusion_codes[present]), present)
  joint <- imap(structure_wide, \(w, ill) {
    w <- filter(w, Participant %in% shared)
    z <- as.data.frame(scale(w[dim_vars]))
    names(z) <- paste0(codes[dim_vars], suffixes[[ill]])
    bind_cols(Participant = w$Participant, z)
  }) |>
    reduce(inner_join, by = "Participant")
  fit_configural <- fit_cfa(cfa_syntax(suffixes), joint)
  fit_metric <- fit_cfa(cfa_syntax(suffixes, equal = TRUE), joint)
  test <- lavaan::lavTestLRT(fit_configural, fit_metric)
  bind_rows(mutate(fit_indices(fit_configural), Model = "Configural"),
            mutate(fit_indices(fit_metric), Model = "Metric")) |>
    mutate(Chisq_diff = c(NA, test$`Chisq diff`[2]), Df_diff = c(NA, test$`Df diff`[2]),
           p = c(NA, test$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]), Delta_CFI = CFI - CFI[1]) |>
    relocate(Model) |>
    gt() |>
    tab_header(title = "Invariance across illusions",
               subtitle = paste0("CFA of every illusion's variables, ", length(shared), " participants")) |>
    cols_label(Model = "", Chisq_diff = "Δχ² (scaled)", Df_diff = "Δdf", Delta_CFI = "ΔCFI") |>
    fmt_number(c(CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR, Chisq_diff, Delta_CFI, p), decimals = 3) |>
    sub_missing() |>
    gt_style()
}
```

### Dimension Scores Across Illusions

Each participant's score on each dimension, from each illusion's own CFA
(the regression method), correlated across illusions over the participants
in both models (Spearman). Each illusion's scores come from its own model,
not from the joint one above. Regression scores in the joint model would be
predicted partly from the other illusions' variables, which would inflate
their correlations across illusions.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6

# Every participant's scores, per illusion (none from a CFA that did not
# converge)
scores <- imap_dfr(cfa_fits, \(f, ill) {
  if (!lavaan::lavInspect(f, "converged")) return(NULL)
  as_tibble(lavaan::lavPredict(f, method = "regression")) |>
    mutate(Participant = structure_wide[[ill]]$Participant[lavaan::lavInspect(f, "case.idx")],
           Illusion_Type = ill)
})

if (length(present) < 2 || length(shared) < min_shared) {
  message("Correlating the scores across illusions needs at least ", min_shared,
          " participants in every model (", length(shared), " now): the full fits.")
} else {
  score_wide <- scores |>
    filter(Participant %in% shared) |>
    pivot_longer(starts_with("D"), names_to = "Dimension", values_to = "Score") |>
    mutate(Variable = paste0(illusion_codes[Illusion_Type], " ", Dimension)) |>
    select(Participant, Variable, Score) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Variable, values_from = Score)
  # Grouped by dimension, then illusion
  vars_scores <- as.vector(outer(illusion_codes[present], names(dims), \(i, k) paste0(i, " D", k)))
  r_scores <- cor(score_wide[vars_scores], method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  as.data.frame(r_scores) |>
    rownames_to_column("Variable1") |>
    pivot_longer(-Variable1, names_to = "Variable2", values_to = "r") |>
    mutate(Label = if_else(Variable1 == Variable2, "", sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf("%.2f", r))),
           Variable1 = factor(Variable1, levels = rev(vars_scores)),
           Variable2 = factor(Variable2, levels = vars_scores)) |>
    ggplot(aes(Variable2, Variable1, fill = r)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Label), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1565C0", mid = "white", high = "#C62828", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "rho") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Dimension scores across illusions",
         subtitle = paste0("Spearman correlations, ", length(shared), " participants; ",
                           paste(dim_labels, collapse = ", "))) +
    coord_equal() +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
}
```
